reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Scriver's OMMBID
clinicalPearls: Distinguished by a severe skeletal dysplasia with markedly short trunk and normal intelligence, setting it apart from most other mucopolysaccharidoses
Two subtypes exist: type A from N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase deficiency and type B from beta-galactosidase deficiency
Atlantoaxial instability with odontoid hypoplasia is a hallmark and poses a major risk of cervical cord compression
Keratan sulfate is the principal accumulated and excreted glycosaminoglycan
Genu valgum, pectus carinatum, kyphoscoliosis, and ligamentous laxity are characteristic
Corneal clouding and hearing loss occur, but cognition is preserved
Diagnosis relies on the specific enzyme assay supported by urinary keratan sulfate, with molecular confirmation
reference.pathophysiology: Morquio syndrome is caused by deficiency of enzymes needed to degrade keratan sulfate. In type A, biallelic GALNS variants cause deficiency of N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase; in type B, GLB1 variants cause deficiency of beta-galactosidase. The resulting block in keratan sulfate (and, in type A, also chondroitin-6-sulfate) degradation leads to lysosomal accumulation, which disproportionately affects cartilage and bone and produces the distinctive spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia. Because keratan sulfate is concentrated in cartilage and cornea rather than the brain, intelligence is characteristically normal. Excess keratan sulfate is excreted in the urine, though levels can normalise with age. Both subtypes are inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
additionalDifferentials: Other mucopolysaccharidoses, particularly Maroteaux-Lamy syndrome (MPS VI)
Other primary skeletal dysplasias with short trunk
GM1 gangliosidosis (allelic with Morquio B through GLB1)
Achondroplasia and other disproportionate short-stature syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Enzyme assay for N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase or beta-galactosidase
Cervical spine imaging including flexion-extension views to assess atlantoaxial instability and odontoid hypoplasia
Skeletal survey to characterise the dysplasia
Echocardiography, ophthalmology, and audiology for extraskeletal involvement
redFlags: Atlantoaxial instability with signs of cervical myelopathy
Respiratory compromise from thoracic cage deformity and airway narrowing
Anaesthetic risk from a difficult airway and unstable cervical spine
reference.prognosis: Intelligence is preserved and survival into adulthood is usual, but skeletal complications, especially cervical instability and restrictive respiratory disease, cause significant morbidity and can be life-threatening if unrecognised. Enzyme replacement therapy is available for type A and may improve endurance and some somatic features.
pitfalls: Failing to screen for atlantoaxial instability before any anaesthetic or surgical procedure
Mistaking the disorder for a primary skeletal dysplasia without measuring glycosaminoglycans
Missing Morquio B because of overlap with GM1 gangliosidosis phenotypes
Assuming normal urinary keratan sulfate excludes the diagnosis in older patients
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Disease-specific enzyme replacement therapy with elosulfase alfa for type A disease

Cervical spine surveillance with flexion-extension imaging and timely surgical stabilisation or decompression for atlantoaxial instability and odontoid hypoplasia, given the risk of cervical cord compression
Respiratory monitoring for restrictive and obstructive disease and sleep-disordered breathing, with airway and ventilatory support as needed
Careful anaesthetic planning for any procedure because of cervical instability and a difficult airway
Orthopaedic management of genu valgum, kyphoscoliosis and joint problems, with physiotherapy and mobility aids
Regular ophthalmology for corneal clouding, audiology for hearing loss and cardiac surveillance for valve disease
Multidisciplinary metabolic and genetics-led care with genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance and family testing
